messages.author: 00f2debfd588b763
messages.subject: obj versus opt
parts:
Working with results from an optimized model can get a little confusing. First you make an object representing you model that can be used to calculate the value of the likelihood function and its gradients etc.

obj <- MakeADFun(data,sim_param,DLL="PTss",random=c("logB","logF"),map = list(m=factor(NA),logB1=factor(NA),logsd_ratio=factor(NA),logsd_catch=factor(NA)))

Then you optimize that function to get the results

opt <- nlminb(obj$par,obj$fn,obj$gr,lower=bounds_lower,upper=bounds_upper)

Now you have two objects, obj and opt, and you have to be careful about where you get the results from. For example

obj$par does not equal opt$par because obj$par is the parameters used to call MakeADFun not the optimized ones.

However, obj$fn() = opt$objective (sometimes) because the default argment of obj$fn() are the optimized parameters (e.g. x = last.par[-random]). Note that this equals obj$fn(opt$par), but not obj$fn(obj$par).

The note at the bottom of the R documentation for MakeADFun warns against using the default output of any of the functions from an object created by MakeADFun and supply the parameters that you want to use (e.g. obj$fn(opt$par)). 

However
obj$report() works but obj$report(obj$par) and obj$report(opt$par) produce the error

Error in f(par, order = 0, type = "double") : Wrong parameter length

but obj$fn(opt$par) works.

apparently the argments for obj$report() are par = last.par, so it will give you the optimised results if used correctly, but to explicitly give it a parameter list you need to include the random effects. nlminb does not appear to provide the parameter list with random effects estimates.

So the questions are
1) how to get the parameter estimates including the random effects 
2) how to get the correct values from the report() function.

Thanks,

Mark

messages.author: 72c025ccfc1fb009
messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] obj versus opt
parts:
obj$report() expects both fixed effects and random effects, compared to obj$gr() and obj$fn() which just expect the fixed effects. I tend to use obj$env$last.par.best to access both fixed and random effect parameters. And pass to the report following.
obj$report(obj$env$last.par.best)

rather than
obj$report(obj$env$last.par)
I don't always trust the last value is the minimum.

To check if the parameters you are passing to the report are the ones that yielded the optimum. I tend to compare the log likelihood from the opt object

opt$objective
with
obj$fn(obj$env$last.par.best[-obj$env$random]) 

The other method to get both fixed and random effect estimate values is through the auxiliary function
sdreport()

Sorry I may have confused myself earlier. The below code should be the same which would return the marginal Log Likelihood
obj$fn(opt$par) == opt$objective
where as the following code, assuming ans defines the joint likelihood
obj$report(obj$env$last.par)$ans  
would return the joint Log Likelihood, which if its a mixed effect model won't be equivalent, as there is the Laplace approximation adjustment for the marginal log-likelihood.

Hopefully I have got that correct.

Working with results from an optimized model can get a little confusing. First you make an object representing you model that can be used to calculate the value of the likelihood function and its gradients etc.

obj <- MakeADFun(data,sim_param,DLL="PTss",random=c("logB","logF"),map = list(m=factor(NA),logB1=factor(NA),logsd_ratio=factor(NA),logsd_catch=factor(NA)))

Then you optimize that function to get the results

opt <- nlminb(obj$par,obj$fn,obj$gr,lower=bounds_lower,upper=bounds_upper)

Now you have two objects, obj and opt, and you have to be careful about where you get the results from. For example

obj$par does not equal opt$par because obj$par is the parameters used to call MakeADFun not the optimized ones.

However, obj$fn() = opt$objective (sometimes) because the default argment of obj$fn() are the optimized parameters (e.g. x = last.par[-random]). Note that this equals obj$fn(opt$par), but not obj$fn(obj$par).

The note at the bottom of the R documentation for MakeADFun warns against using the default output of any of the functions from an object created by MakeADFun and supply the parameters that you want to use (e.g. obj$fn(opt$par)). 

However
obj$report() works but obj$report(obj$par) and obj$report(opt$par) produce the error

Error in f(par, order = 0, type = "double") : Wrong parameter length

but obj$fn(opt$par) works.

apparently the argments for obj$report() are par = last.par, so it will give you the optimised results if used correctly, but to explicitly give it a parameter list you need to include the random effects. nlminb does not appear to provide the parameter list with random effects estimates.

So the questions are
1) how to get the parameter estimates including the random effects 
2) how to get the correct values from the report() function.
